# Epistle of Barnabas — Chapter 18 (EMET Literal)

**Source:** Codex Sinaiticus, Epistle of Barnabas 18
**Agent:** EMET (Literal)
**Date:** 2026-03-17

---

1. The way of light is this: if anyone wishes to travel to the appointed place, he should be diligent in his works. The knowledge given to us for walking in this way is as follows:
2. You shall love your maker; you shall fear your creator; you shall glorify him who redeemed you from death. You shall be simple in heart and rich in spirit. You shall not cleave to those who walk the way of death. You shall hate all that is not pleasing to God; you shall hate all hypocrisy. You shall not abandon the commandments of the Lord.
3. You shall not exalt yourself, but shall be humble in all things. You shall not take glory to yourself. You shall not form a malicious plan against your neighbor. You shall not give your heart to arrogance.
4. You shall not commit fornication; you shall not commit adultery; you shall not corrupt children. The word of God shall not go out from you to anyone who is unclean. You shall not accept persons in rebuking someone for a transgression. You shall be meek. You shall be quiet. You shall tremble at the words you have heard.
5. You shall not hold a grudge against your brother. You shall not be double-minded as to whether a thing shall be or not. You shall not take the name of God in vain. You shall love your neighbor more than your own soul. You shall not murder a child by abortion, nor again shall you kill it after it is born. You shall not withhold your hand from your son or from your daughter, but from their youth you shall teach them the fear of God.
6. You shall not covet your neighbor's goods; you shall not be avaricious. You shall not be one who is joined to the haughty, but shall walk with the humble and righteous. You shall receive as good the things that befall you, knowing that nothing happens without God.
7. You shall not be double-tongued or double-minded; for a double-tongue is a snare of death. You shall be subject to the Lord and to human lords as an image of God, with reverence and fear.
8. Whatever commandment is given you, keep them, neither adding anything to them nor taking from them.
